title: Comparative effectiveness of levothyroxine, desiccated thyroid extract, and levothyroxine+liothyronine in hypothyroidism
authors: Shakir MKM, Brooks DI, McAninch EA, Fonseca TL, Mai VQ, Bianco AC, et al.
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
population: Hypothyroid patients at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, excluding cardiac disease, malabsorption and use of psychotropic drugs, iron, sucralfate and proton pump inhibitors
funder: Provided by Walter Reed National Military Medical Center Institutional Research Board.
authorConflicts: A.B. is a consultant for Synthonics, BLA Technology and Allergan; the other authors declared no competing financial interests.
result: Double-blind crossover of levothyroxine, levothyroxine plus liothyronine and desiccated thyroid extract. TSH stayed within the reference range in all arms; thyroid symptoms, general health questionnaire, memory and depression scores and treatment preference did not differ, except a minor rise in heart rate on desiccated extract; DIO2 Thr92Ala and aetiology did not modify outcomes. In a subgroup analysis of the third most symptomatic on levothyroxine, patients preferred and scored better on T3-containing treatment; the number homozygous for the DIO2 variant was likely too small for meaningful evaluation.
